stock.source: HazeGuard-MY brief default; placeholder, not real MOH stock

allocation.clinic_rule: one mobile clinic per state in priority order until clinics run out
allocation.n95_rule: states with priority <= n95_max_priority share the N95 stock in proportion to vulnerable people (label.vulnerable_weights), capped at n95_per_vulnerable_person each; rounding leftovers go to the most urgent state first

label.grades_note: 16 = one grade per state, i.e. the full within-year order of the harm proxy. With 4 (quartiles) the top four states tie, so the ranker never learns their order and barely reacts to the forecast.
label.description: PROXY, not ground truth. harm = exposure x vulnerable people, graded by within-year quantile of harm (highest grade = most harm).
label.exposure_note: Mean daily PM2.5 rather than unhealthy-day count: CAMS reads ~40 ug/m3 over the Klang Valley, just above the 35 ug/m3 threshold, so day counts there are inflated ~10-300x vs other states.
label.source: Team assumption: no official haze-priority list exists; poor households weighted 2x because exposure correlates with income (rho ~0.7)

baseline_weights.source: HazeGuard-MY brief: weighted index (low median income 0.4, 65+ 0.2, under-5 0.2, low beds 0.2) on within-year z-scores
